stages.title: Limits of supply-side policy and the Phillips curve conflict
stages.sub: After this the student can explain why supply-side policy can fail without demand, and why cutting unemployment can raise inflation.

steps.q: A government funds new training schemes and roads, shifting LRAS rightward. Firms now have more capacity to produce. But if households and firms are not buying any more than before, will firms actually produce up to that new capacity?
steps.right: No, they will only produce what is being bought
steps.wrong: Yes, firms always produce at full capacity
steps.hint: Think about why a factory would increase output: does having the ability to produce more mean people are buying more?

steps.q: Given that the new capacity is going unused, what else would need to happen for output to actually rise to meet it?
steps.right: Demand would need to rise as well
steps.hint: Capacity is the ceiling. What has to increase for actual output to reach that ceiling?

steps.q: A country builds new factories and trains workers, but consumers keep spending the same amount as before. Will national output rise by as much as the supply-side policy intended?
steps.right: No, it will fall short without extra demand
steps.wrong: Yes, output always rises to match new capacity
steps.hint: Think back to the unused capacity: does building it guarantee it gets used?
